note: Adapted from Holmgren's 1906 original German description; the original reads Eutermes convexifrons n. sp., an original description (new species). The original ends by noting that this species is a primary-forest dweller, tunnelling in the ground, that soldiers are not especially numerous, that the swarming period is December (month 12), and that the locality is Chaquimayo (Carabaya Province, Peru). The soldier head width is printed in the original as 0.2 mm, which is inconsistent with the abdomen width 0.87 mm and head length 1.48 mm in the same description and is probably a misprint for 0.82; this entry follows the original and notes the discrepancy. The original figures A, B, C show the heads (and mandibles) of the alate, soldier and worker respectively, at a scale of 23:1.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body length with wings 8.5 mm, body length without wings 6 mm; head length 0.81 mm, head width 0.74 mm. Head, thorax and abdominal segments greyish brown. Head, tergites and sternites quite densely hairy, almost without long setae. Head (original fig. A-a) rounded behind the compound eyes, triangularly pointed in front of the eyes. Frontal gland pore oval, placed far back. Ocelli round. Frontal suture indistinct, coronal suture almost only a trace. Frontal band with a pale spot on each side. Postclypeus with its posterior margin angularly bent, anterior margin evenly concave; the basal part has a longitudinal groove; the distal part is lens-shaped. Labrum long, rather narrow, protruding beak-like. Mandible distal part overlapping the basal part rather distinctly, as in Anoplotermes; right mandible (fig. A-b) with traces of two points on the basal margin, left mandible with weakly developed basal tooth; first apical tooth of both mandibles larger than the second. Wings transparent, greyish black (smoky): forewing with 2 veins from the media, 13 from the submedia, of which the inner 7 are thickened; hindwing with 3 veins from the media, 11 from the submedia, of which the inner 7 are thickened; venation variable in both wings. Wing scales small. Pronotum transverse, oval, about twice as wide as long. Abdomen of equal width and long. Legs short, femora and tibiae slightly flattened.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 2.9 mm; head length 1.48 mm; head width 0.2 mm (sic; probably a misprint for 0.82). Head rusty yellow, the tip of the frontal projection rusty brown. Head densely covered with short, stiff, microscopic hairs, with 2—3 longer setae on the frons. Thorax, abdomen and legs straw yellow; grey-black intestinal contents visible through the abdomen. Abdominal tergites densely covered with short fine hairs, without long setae; the posterior margins of the sternites bear additional longer setae directed forwards. Head (figs B-a, B-b) round, frontal projection conical, rather short; frontal outline fairly evenly convex. Antennae 11-segmented, segment 2 shorter than segment 3, segment 3 slightly longer than or equal to segment 4. Pronotum saddle-shaped. Abdomen narrow (0.87 mm), narrower than the head.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 4.2 mm; head length 1 mm, head width 0.81 mm. Head pale straw yellow, densely covered with almost microscopic short hairs and a few longer setae. Thoracic segments with short hairs. Abdomen long, cylindrical, pale greyish white, grey-black intestinal contents visible through it. Tergites hairy, without long setae; the posterior margins of the sternites bear a few additional long setae directed forwards. Head (fig. C-a) round, widest in front of the antennae. Frons with a distinct longitudinal suture, coronal suture not visible. Basal part of the clypeus swollen, with a median groove. Labrum ligulate. Right mandible (fig. C-b) with the median tooth near the second apical tooth; left mandible with a fine notch at the second apical tooth; basal tooth with 2 rounded points. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 equal in length to segment 4. Anterior margin of the pronotum upturned.
